question.prompt: If \(\dfrac mn=\dfrac43\) and \(\dfrac rt=\dfrac9{14},\) the value of \(\dfrac{3mr-nt}{4nt-7mr}\) is:

solutions.explanation:
Both parts of the expression involve only \(mr\) and \(nt\), so first find their ratio. The given fractions require \(n\ne0\) and \(t\ne0\), and
\[
\frac{mr}{nt}=\frac mn\cdot\frac rt
=\frac43\cdot\frac9{14}=\frac67.
\]
Consequently, \(4nt-7mr=(4-6)nt=-2nt\ne0\), so the requested expression is defined. Dividing its numerator and denominator by \(nt\) gives
\[
\frac{3mr-nt}{4nt-7mr}
=\frac{3\left(\frac67\right)-1}{4-7\left(\frac67\right)}
=\frac{11/7}{-2}
=-\frac{11}{14}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{-\frac{11}{14}}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Use the ratio of the products
